banked_cloze.overview: 本文节选自Discovery探索频道网站上2020年12月2日发表的一篇标题为"Secret Tunnels Beneath the Desert"的文章。本文主要讲述了莫哈韦沙漠的独特地理风貌和自然环境。在作者看来，它是户外爱好者和摄影师的理想之地。
banked_cloze.fullTextTranslation:
沙漠具有欺骗性。乍一看，它看起来毫无生气、贫瘠且干燥至极。对于大多数去拉斯维加斯碰运气或者前往大峡谷、在路上哼着歌穿过莫哈韦的路人来说，这只是一片[26]平坦之地，远处有一些山脉，更[27]容易作为一部发生在火星上的电影的场景。然而，这片沙漠却[28]充满了生命、神秘和魔力。
莫哈韦沙漠每年的降雨量不足两英寸，和大多数沙漠一样，这里也是一片[29]极端之地。温度波动的范围从严寒到[30]酷热不等，不仅在季节之间，甚至在同一天内也是如此。
莫哈韦国家保护区位于这片25,000平方英里广阔沙漠的中心。在那里管理和工作的人都戴着宽边帽，这已经成为约塞米蒂这样的地方的[31]代名词。该保护区拥有丰富的历史、文化、生物多样性和无尽的机会来[32]激发你的兴趣，尤其是对于任何热爱户外活动的人来说。对于摄影师来说，要想驾驭这些未铺设的"道路"网络，不仅需要耐心，还[33]可能需要一些备用轮胎，但回报是丰厚的。
在这里拍摄需要一双[34]结实的好鞋和大量的准备工作。要探索这个国家公园系统中的第三大公园，需要大量的水、备用轮胎和满满一箱汽油。
然而，就像所有的沙漠一样，如果你有耐心，你会得到回报，因为它们往往会慢慢地揭示自己的秘密。在我上次旅行中，我惊讶地发现这一地区的很多地方都是由古火山和地质力量塑造而成的，其中大部分至今仍保留着，这给该地区带来了一种[35]独特的感觉，也为拍摄绝佳照片提供了丰富多彩的背景。

information_matching.overview: 本文节选自美国《经济学人》杂志于2020年3月发表的一篇标题为"African countries must get smarter with their agriculture"的文章。气候变化影响到地球上的每一个人，但对非洲人来说，气候变化的后果将尤其严重。部分原因在于它本身已经很难养活自己，必须大幅提高产量和生产力。但从长远来看，要真正让非洲农民摆脱贫困，能支付得起医疗和教育费用，则需要工厂和城市提供更好的工作；农业能起到的作用有限。
information_matching.fullTextTranslation:
非洲国家必须在农业方面变得更加智能
A) 在肯尼亚中部的山丘上，阳光下茶树闪闪发光，呈现出近似石灰绿的颜色，这里的农民对气候变化了如指掌。其中一人说："已经无法预测雨季了。在应该下雨的时候，却没有下雨，后面雨又一下子都来了。" [43]气候变化是一个会影响地球上每一个人的问题。对非洲人来说，其后果将尤其严重：当其他地区能够通过燃烧煤炭和石油致富时，非洲将在没有享受到好处的情况下付出巨大的人力代价。管理世界银行80亿美元气候投资基金的马法尔达·杜阿尔特说："非洲排放的温室气体只占全球温室气体排放量的2%，但预计它是受气候变化最严重的一个洲。"
B) 尽管气候变化的确切影响有很大的不确定性，但我们了解得足够多，足以可以说全球变暖是（阻碍）非洲繁荣的主要威胁之一。[38]非洲大陆部分地区的变暖速度已经远超全球平均水平：在过去的50年里，非洲南部的气温上升速度大约是全球的两倍。即使世界减少的排放量足以将全球气温上升幅度控制在1.5℃以内，非洲的热浪也会加剧，疾病也会蔓延到目前尚未受到影响的地区。农业也将受到重创。现在用于种植玉米的土地中约有40%将不再适合种植。总体而言，玉米产量估计将下降18%~22%。
C) [40]非洲尤其容易受到影响，部分原因在于它本身已经很难养活自己，如果要为其快速增长的人口提供食物，即便没有气候变化，它也必须大幅提高产量和生产力。联合国粮农组织估计，到2050年，全球粮食产量必须在2009年的基础上增长约70%，才能满足人口数量和食欲不断增长的需求。大部分的新需求将来自非洲。然而，非洲大陆每年进口价值约500亿美元的食品，预计这一数字在未来5年将增加一倍以上。自给自足并不是非洲的目标，但它在进口食品上的支出比在购买资本货物上的支出要多，这一事实表明它还有提升的空间。
D) 找出原因并不难。大多数农场都很小，靠人工耕种，依赖雨水。非洲一半以上的人口以务农为生。尽管在过去的几十年里，非洲的粮食总产量有所上升，但这主要是因为有更多的人在耕种更多的土地。但在许多地方，没有多余的土地可供耕种。卢旺达的耕地小到一个普通的美国农场里能装250块。[44]尽管非洲的人均（农业）产量在过去30年里提高了一半以上，但仍远远落后于亚洲2.5倍的增幅。玉米产量一般每公顷不到两吨，是美国五分之一。
E) 非洲农民的生产率体现在了国家经济统计数据中——[36]尽管吸收了如此多的劳动力，农业只创造了15%的国内生产总值。非洲开发银行负责农业的副行长詹妮弗·布兰克说："他们甚至无法养活自己的家庭。[36] 100年来，非洲许多地区的农业生产力没有提高。"
F) 一个原因是，在非洲独立的最初几十年里，多个非洲国家的政府把重点放在了经济工业化上，而忽视了农业。另一些国家则通过压低国有垄断企业购买农作物的价格，以补贴城市工人，让他们能以低价购买食品，以致对农业造成了破坏。在20世纪60年代至80年代期间，加纳对可可粉出口课以重税，导致产量暴跌了一半，而当时全球的可可粉价格却在暴涨。然而，在过去20年左右的时间里，政府和捐助者已经开始重新将农业视为每年为1,300万进入劳动力市场的年轻人提供就业机会的一种方式。[41]焦点主要集中在让小农使用肥料上，更重要的是，用更好的种子。效果十分显著。例如，高粱的改良品种的产量可以比普通品种的产量高出40%。基础设施很重要。世界银行在埃塞俄比亚的一个灌溉项目帮助农民将马铃薯的产量从每公顷8吨提高到了35吨。
G) [39]更好的技术也有帮助。肯尼亚的咖啡种植小农只需遵循一些简单的指导原则来打理他们的树丛，比如修剪咖啡树枝，只保留三根枝条，他们的收入就能增加40%。他们的许多邻居都不听从这个建议，因为这似乎有违直觉。他们说，更多的枝条应该会长出更多的咖啡豆。然而，在看到那些遵循建议的人在一两季里获得了更多的收成后，许多其他人也开始这样做。
H) [37]传播知识的一种方法是把农场和收购他们收成的大买家联系起来。当英国饮料巨头帝亚吉欧在肯尼亚西部建了一家啤酒厂时，它是想用当地的作物生产出足够便宜的啤酒，与非法的自制啤酒竞争。它将农民组织成小组，改善供应链，让他们获得种子和肥料，然后同意购买他们产出的粮食。现在，它为大约1.7万名农民提供了销售市场。该公司负责非洲业务的约翰·奥基夫说，在整个地区，该公司对当地原材料的使用量在五年内翻了一番，达到了80%左右。
I) [42]一个更重要的转变是从传统农业转向创立能为小农户带来技术和投资，并从中获利的企业。年轻的肯尼亚人泰塔·恩格蒂奇在学习工程学时想要赚点外快。他凑了2万肯尼亚先令（约200美元）来种西红柿，结果进展一点也不顺利。庄稼受到了害虫的侵袭。他说："然后发生了一场大洪水，吞噬了我们所有的启动资金。"恩格蒂奇先生考虑到买一个温室大棚，以保护他的作物免受昆虫和雨水的侵害。最便宜的温室大棚单价要超过2,500美元，所以他花一半的钱自己做了一个。很快，附近的农民开始向他下订单，现在在他的公司"Illuminum温室大棚"已经卖出了1,400多个温室大棚，为大约6,000人提供了生计。他的生意还不止于此；他还供应肥料、优质的幼苗和能提高产量的智能传感器。
J) Illuminum公司的成功表明，技术甚至可以帮助小农场提高生产力。由于非洲如此大规模的人口以农业为生，因此即使生产力的小幅提升也能提高数百万人的收入。[45]但从更长远来看，小规模农业只能起到一定作用，尤其是在面对气候变化和人口压力的情况下。
K) 恩格蒂奇先生说："如果我们真的想让人们摆脱贫困，我们就必须资助那些能提供月收入至少100美元的项目，这样他们就能支付得起医疗和教育费用。那些通过种植豆类或玉米每月付给他们额外2美元的项目无法让他们实现这一目标。"要实现这些飞跃，需要工厂和城市提供更好的就业机会。

careful_reading::passage_one.overview: 本文节选自《纽约时报》于2020年11月发表的一篇标题为"Let's Talk About Higher Wages"的文章。文章指出，虽然近几十年来，美国共和党一直宣传减税可以促进经济增长，但其实并未取得成效，现在应该转而关注提高工资，通过提高工资拉动消费，从而带动经济增长。
careful_reading::passage_one.fullTextTranslation:
近几十年来，共和党最大的成功之一就是坚持不懈地宣传一个简单的经济增长方案：减税。
[46]这个方案虽然不起作用，但这并没有影响它的受欢迎程度。对减税的推崇引来了许多批评人士，但它缺乏明显的竞争对手。
民主党政客倾向于宣传帮助那些被经济增长抛在后面的人。当民主党人真的谈论鼓励经济增长时，他们的话往往听起来像共和党人。
这不仅仅是民主党人的政治问题，也是美国的经济问题。关于经济增长动力，美国需要一个更好的故事。[47]近几十年的惨痛教训指向了一个大有可为的候选方案：提高工资。
提高美国工人的工资应该成为经济政策制定者的首要任务。我们最好减少对国内生产总值（GDP）季度增长最新消息的关注，转而关注工人工资的增长。
暂且抛开人们熟悉的提高工资的理由：公平。这里要说的理由是，提高工资可以推动经济增长。
也许最著名的提高工资带来好处的例子是亨利·福特在1914年决定向其T型车装配线上的工人支付5美元的日薪。他这样做是为了提高产量——是在为维持一支可靠的劳动队伍支付附加费。意外的好处是，福特工厂的工人也成了福特的客户。
[48]同样的逻辑仍然成立：消费推动美国经济的发展，工资更高的工人消费也会更高。
主流经济学家坚持认为，不可能要求工资持续增长，因为薪酬水平反映的是对市场力量的准确判断。
[49]传统观点认为，生产率增长是提高工资的唯一途径。从这个角度来看，商定更高工资的努力只会适得其反。最低工资法会增加失业率，因为工资池中只有这么多钱，如果一些人得到更多，其他人就什么也得不到。
正是在这种世界观的背景下，减税可以推动（经济）繁荣的论调开始流行起来。富人会投资，生产率会提高，工资会上涨。
在现实世界中，情况更为复杂。工资受到雇主和工人之间激烈争夺的影响，而获胜的一直是雇主。[50]一个明显的证据是，自大约1970年以来，生产率增幅与工资增幅之间的差距不断扩大。生产率增长了一倍多，而工资增长却远远落后。
对工资增长的关注，将矫正人们对减税具有神奇力量的信念，这种信念简单且有吸引力。

careful_reading::passage_two.overview: 本文节选自The British Psychological Society（英国心理学会）网站于2022年2月22日发表的一篇标题为"The majority of psychology journal editors are men and based in the US"的文章。文章指出，《自然—神经科学》杂志上的一项新研究发现，顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑都是男性，这可能会加剧该领域存在的性别不平等，并影响发表的研究的类型。文章继续指出，编委会的性别不平等问题并不是缺乏女性学者导致的，而是现实存在一些不利于女性的障碍，积极打破这些障碍有助于实现期刊编辑的多样性。
careful_reading::passage_two.fullTextTranslation:
期刊编辑决定着发表什么，不发表什么，这影响着其他学者的职业生涯，也影响着一个领域的发展方向。[51]那么，人们会希望期刊尽其所能建立一个多元化的编委会，反映各种声音、经历和身份。
不幸的是，《自然—神经科学》杂志上的一项新研究读起来让人沮丧。[52]该研究团队发现，顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑都是男性，而且都在美国：这种情况可能会加剧该领域存在的性别不平等，并影响发表的研究的类型。
研究发现，在心理学期刊的编辑中，男性占60%。在各个级别的编辑中，男性编辑都明显多于女性编辑，而且超过四分之三的期刊中，男性编辑占大多数。[53]至关重要地，女性编辑的比例明显低于女性心理学研究人员的总体比例。
神经科学期刊中的差异更为明显：70%的编辑是男性，88%的期刊中男性占据了大多数编辑职位。在此情况下，女性编辑的比例并不显著低于从事神经科学工作的女性研究人员的比例——这一发现更广泛地揭示了该领域长期存在的性别差异问题。
[54]根据他们的研究结果，该团队得出结论："在心理学和神经科学领域最知名的学术期刊中，男性的想法、价值观和决策偏好在编辑职位上被过度代表了。"
在科学界，性别不平等通常被归因于高级学者更有可能是男性这个事实，因为历史上科学是男性主导的：有人认为，随着时间的推移，越来越多的女性升至高级职位，这一领域将变得更加平等。然而，这项研究表明，尽管女性初级心理从业人员的人数实际上多于男性，但即使是心理学期刊的初级职位也往往不成比例地由男性占据。
这意味着缺乏女性学者不是问题所在。[55]相反，女性在科学领域处于不利地位是有结构性原因的。例如，女性的工资较低，面临更大的育儿需求，这可能会导致其发表的论文和获得的经费较少——期刊在决定任命谁时会考虑这些因素。[55]我们不应该简单地将编委会的不平等归咎于传统，而应该积极打破这些现有的障碍。
期刊编辑缺乏多样性也可能是造成心理学"WEIRD"问题的原因之一。如果期刊编辑大多是来自美国的男性，那么他们可能会有意无意地更看重与西方、男性群体相关的论文。
【编者注】WEIRD这个缩写代表了"Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic"，描述了在心理学研究中常用的样本特征。这些研究样本通常来自于西方、受过教育的、工业化的、富裕的民主国家，而这种偏好使得人们可能陷入了一个局限的视角。

passage.title: African countries must get smarter with their agriculture

paragraphs.text: On the hills of central Kenya, almost lime-green with the sparkle of tea bushes in the sunlight, farmers know all about climate change. "The rainy season is no longer predictable," says one. "When it is supposed to rain it doesn't, then it all comes at once." Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet. For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter: whereas other regions were able to grow rich by burning coal and oil, Africa will pay much of the human price without having enjoyed the benefits. "Africa only represents 2% of global greenhouse-gas emissions but it is the continent that is expected to suffer the most from climate impacts," says Mafalda Duarte, who runs the World Bank's $8bn Climate Investment Funds.

Although there are huge uncertainties as to the precise impacts of climate change, enough is known to say that global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa's prosperity. Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years. Even if the world were to cut emissions enough to keep global warming below 1.5℃, heat-waves would intensify in Africa and diseases would spread to areas not currently affected. Farming would also be hit hard. About 40% of the land now used to grow maize (玉米) would no longer be suitable for it. Overall, it is estimated that maize yields would fall by 18-22%.

Africa is particularly vulnerable, in part because it is already struggling to feed itself and it will have to vastly increase yields and productivity if it is to put food on the plates of a fast-growing population, even without climate change. The UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation reckons that by 2050 global food production would have to rise by about 70% over its level of 2009 to meet demand from a population that is growing in numbers and appetite. Much of this new demand will be in Africa. Yet the continent already imports about $50bn-worth of food a year and that figure is expected to more than double over the next five years. Self-sufficiency is not Africa's goal, but the fact that it spends more money importing food than it does buying capital goods suggests it has room for improvement.

Finding out why is not hard. Most farms are tiny, ploughed by hand and reliant on rain. More than half of Africa's people make their living from farming. Although its total harvest has climbed over the past few decades, this is mainly because there are more people farming more land. But in many places there is no spare land to farm. Plots in Rwanda are so small that you could fit 250 of them onto the average American farm. And although output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia. Yields of maize are generally less than two tonnes per hectare, a fifth the level in America.

The low productivity of African farmers is reflected in national economic statistics—despite absorbing so much labour, farming generates just 15% of GDP. "They can't even feed their families," says Jennifer Blanke, a vice-president of the African Development Bank in charge of agriculture. "Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years."

One reason is that in the first few decades of independence, many African governments neglected farming as they focused on industrialising their economies. Others damaged it by pushing down the prices that state monopolies paid for their crops in order to subsidise workers in cities with cheap food. Ghana taxed cocoa (可可粉) exports so heavily that production collapsed by half between the 1960s and 1980s, despite a jump in the global price of cocoa. Yet over the past two decades or so governments and donors have begun to look again at farming as a way of providing jobs for the 13 million young people entering the workforce each year. Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds. The results can be impressive. Improved varieties of sorghum (高粱), for instance, can produce a crop that is 40%larger than the usual variety. Infrastructure is important. A World Bank irrigation project in Ethiopia helped farmers increase their potato harvest from about 8 tonnes per hectare to 35 tonnes.

Better techniques help, too. Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems. Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice, because it seems counter-intuitive. More stems ought to lead to more coffee beans, they say. Yet after seeing those following the advice get bigger harvests for a season or two, many others start doing the same.

One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests. When Diageo, a British drinks giant, built a brewery in western Kenya, it wanted to use local crops to make a beer cheap enough to compete with illicit home brew. It organised farmers into groups, improved supply chains for them to get seeds and fertiliser and then agreed to buy their grain. It now provides a market to about 17,000 farmers. Across the region it has doubled its use of local raw material to about 80% over five years, says John O'Keeffe, who runs its Africa business.

An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers. Taita Ngetich, a young Kenyan, was studying engineering when he wanted to earn a little money on the side. He scraped together 20,000 Kenyan shillings (about $200) to plant tomatoes. Everything went wrong. The crop was attacked by pests. "Then there was a massive flood that swallowed all our capital," he says. Mr Ngetich persevered by looking into buying a greenhouse to protect his plants from bugs and rain. The cheapest ones cost more than $2,500 each, so he designed his own for half the price. Soon neighbouring farmers started placing orders with him, and now his firm, Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000people. The business does not stop there; he also supplies fertiliser, high-quality seedlings and smart sensors that increase yields.

Illuminum's success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive. Because such a large share of Africa's population earns a living from agriculture, even small improvements in productivity can lift the incomes of millions of people. But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure.

"If we really want to lift people out of poverty we have to finance projects that will get them an income of at least $100 a month so that they can pay for health care and education," says Mr Ngetich. "Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren't going to get them there." Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities.

blocks.text:
One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts.
The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.
Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans.
This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages.
Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP)and focusing instead on the growth of workers' paychecks.
Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.
Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford's decision in 1914 to pay $5a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too.
The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more.
Mainstream economists insist that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces.
The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none.
It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise.
In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.
A focus on wage growth would provide an antidote (矫正方法) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts.

items.stemEn: Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective?

The cult of tax cuts has been relentlessly propagated by all policymakers.
There appears to be a misunderstanding of the formula among the public.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective可将答案线索定位至第二段。第二段提及，这个方案虽然不起作用，但这并没有影响它的受欢迎程度。对减税的推崇引来了许多批评人士，但它缺乏明显的竞争对手。由此可知，原文所说的"竞争对手"就是指其他解决方案，即没有其他可替代的方案，故答案为B。
review.questionTranslation: 为什么减税方案虽然无效，却仍然受欢迎？

options.text: 其批评者的声音没有传遍全国。
似乎没有其他方案可以取代它。
所有决策者都不停地宣传对减税的推崇。
公众似乎对该方案存在误解。

items.stemEn: What does the author think is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.?

Prioritizing the growth of the nation's GDP.
Increasing the compensation for labor.
Introducing even more extensive tax cuts.

优先考虑国家GDP的增长。
提高劳动报酬。
实行更大规模的减税。

items.stemEn: What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint?

Familiar arguments for higher wages are outdated.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词logic可将答案线索定位至第八段。第八段中作者指出，同样的逻辑仍然成立，即消费推动美国经济的发展，工资更高的工人消费也会更高。也就是说，工资的增长会推动国家经济的发展，因此答案为A。
review.questionTranslation: 作者观点背后的逻辑是什么？

options.text: 工人工资的增长最终会推动国家经济的发展。
支付附加费来维持可靠的劳动力队伍吸引了更多的客户。
消费刺激了人们对更高工资的渴望。

items.stemEn: What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom?

options.textEn: Fairness in distribution.
Increase in productivity.
The priority of economic policymakers.
The unerring judgment of market forces.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词conventional wisdom可将答案线索定位至倒数第四段第一句。倒数第四段第一句指出，传统观点认为，生产率增长是提高工资的唯一途径，因此B项符合题意。

生产率的提高。
经济决策者的优先事项。
对市场力量的准确判断。

evidence.location: 定位栏信息词（解析定位栏，原文命中）
evidence.quote: conventional wisdom

items.stemEn: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so?

options.textEn: People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity.
People have been disheartened by the widening gap between the haves and have-nots.
People have witnessed a tug of war between Republicans and Democrats over tax cuts.
People have seen the link disappearing between productivity and workers' well-being.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词real world、the past 50 years or so可将答案线索定位至倒数第二段。倒数第二段开头总结道，在现实世界中，情况更为复杂，工资受到雇主和工人之间激烈争夺的影响，而获胜的一直是雇主。随后说明一个具体论据：大约自1970年以来，生产率增幅与工资增幅之间的差距不断扩大，生产率增长了一倍多，而工资增长却远远落后。由此可知，A项符合题意。
review.questionTranslation: 我们对过去50年左右的时间里美国的现实世界了解到什么？

options.text: 人们没有看到工资和生产率的相应增长。
人们对富人和穷人之间日益扩大的差距感到沮丧。
人们目睹了共和党和民主党在减税问题上的激烈争夺。
人们看到了生产率与工人福利之间的联系正在消失。

evidence.location: 定位栏信息词（解析定位栏，原文命中）
evidence.quote: real world

distractors: 其他三项在倒数第二段中均未体现，故均排除。

blocks.text:
Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.
Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.
Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.
The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience—a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly.
Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience."
Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty.
This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.
A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology's WEIRD problem. If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not.

items.stemEn: What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities?

options.textEn: Insight.
Expertise.
Integrity.
Diversity.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词an editorial board of an academic journal可将答案线索定位于第一段。第一段有两句话，第一句提到期刊编辑决定发表的内容，这影响一个领域的发展；第二句指出人们的期望，即希望期刊尽其所能建立一个多元化的编委会，反映各种声音、经历和身份。原文中的diverse和选项D的Diversity基本属于原词复现，由此可知选项D为正确答案。
review.questionTranslation: 鉴于学术期刊编委会的重要职责，我们期望它展现出什么？

options.text: 洞察力。
专业知识。
诚信。
多样性。

evidence.location: 定位栏信息词（解析定位栏，原文命中）
evidence.quote: editorial board

distractors: 其他三个选项均在原文中找不到对应信息，故均排除。

items.stemEn: What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience?

options.textEn: The majority of top psychology and neuroscience journals reflect a variety of voices, experiences and identities.
The editorial boards of most psychology and neuroscience journals do influence the direction their field takes.
The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male-dominated.
The majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals have relevant backgrounds.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience可将答案线索定位于第二段。第二段第二句提到，该研究团队发现，顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑都是男性。很明显，选项C是对该句话的同义转述，其中male-dominated对应原文中的the majority of editors are male，most important对应原文中的top，故选C。
review.questionTranslation: 我们从《自然—神经科学》杂志的一项研究的发现中了解到什么？

options.text: 大多数顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊反映了各种声音、经历和身份。
大多数心理学和神经科学期刊的编委会确实会影响其领域的发展方向。
心理学和神经科学领域最重要的期刊的编委会都以男性为主。
顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑都有相关背景。

evidence.location: 定位栏信息词（解析定位栏，原文命中）
evidence.quote: a new study in Nature Neuroscience

distractors: 选项A与第一段提到的人们对期刊编委会的期望有关，不是研究发现，故排除；选项B是根据第一段第一句所陈述事实所做的推理，也不是研究发现，故排除；选项D在原文中没有相关信息，故排除。

items.stemEn: What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals?

options.textEn: There were quite a few female editors who also distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers.
The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research.
The proportion of female editors was increasingly lower at senior levels.
There were few female editors who could move up to senior positions.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词gender differences in editors of psychology journals可将答案线索定位于第三段。第三段主要阐述了心理学期刊编辑中的性别差异。该段最后一句提到，女性编辑的比例明显低于女性心理学研究人员的总体比例。选项B是对这句话的同义转述，故为正确答案。
review.questionTranslation: 关于心理学期刊编辑的性别差异，作者强调了什么事实？

options.text: 不少女性编辑作为有影响力的心理学研究者而享有盛誉。
女性编辑的人数与从事心理学研究的女性的人数完全不成比例。
高级编辑中女性编辑的比例越来越低。
能晋升到高级职位的女性编辑很少。

distractors: 选项A文中没有提到，比较容易排除；选项C和D是利用原文中的seniority（资历）一词设置的干扰项，在原文中没有对应信息支持，故也排除。

items.stemEn: What can we infer from the conclusion drawn by the team of the new study on the basis of their findings?

options.textEn: Women's views are underrepresented in the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals.
Male editors of top psychology and neuroscience journals tend to be biased against their female colleagues.
Male researchers have enough representation in the editorial boards to ensure their publications.
Female editors have to struggle to get women's research articles published in academic journals.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词the conclusion drawn by the team可将答案线索定位于第五段。第五段引号中的内容就是研究小组根据新发现得出的结论：在心理学和神经科学领域最知名的学术期刊中，男性的想法、价值观和决策偏好在编辑职位上被过度代表了。从另一方面来看，在顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊中，女性编辑占比较小，那么女性的想法、价值观和决策偏好没有在编辑职位上得到充分代表，选项A符合该句推论，故为正确答案。
review.questionTranslation: 从新研究小组根据他们的发现得出的结论中我们能推断出什么？

options.text: 在顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊的编委会中，女性的观点没有得到充分代表。
顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊的男性编辑往往对他们的女性同事有偏见。
男性研究人员在编委会中有足够的代表，确保他们的作品得以发表。
女性编辑必须努力才能争取在学术期刊上发表女性的研究文章。

distractors: 选项B是对原文信息的错误推论，原文说的是男性编辑的想法、价值观和决策偏好被过度代表了，而不是对女性同事存在偏见，故排除。选项C和选项D在原文中没有提到，故均排除。

items.stemEn: What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition?

options.textEn: Strike a balance between male and female editors.
Increase women's employment in senior positions.
Enlarge the body of female academics.
Implement overall structural reforms.

review.explanation: 根据题干信息词blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition可将答案线索定位于第七段。第七段最后一句提到，我们不应该简单地将编委会的不平等归咎于传统，而应该积极打破这些现有的障碍。这些障碍是什么，需要考生往前寻找。该段开头提到女性编辑数量少不是因为缺乏女性学者，其实女性在科学领域处于不利地位是有结构性原因的，随后举例说明，比如女性的工资较低，面临更大的育儿需求，从而导致其发表的论文和获得的经费较少，而论文少、经费低又导致女性学者达不到期刊任命编辑职位的标准，这些就是女性面临的障碍。因此作者建议我们实施整体结构改革，故选项D正确。
review.questionTranslation: 与其简单地将编委会的不平等归咎于传统，作者建议我们做什么？

options.text: 在男性编辑和女性编辑之间取得平衡。
增加女性担任高级职务的人数。
扩大女性学者群体。
实施整体结构改革。

evidence.location: 定位栏信息词（解析定位栏，原文命中）
evidence.quote: blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition

distractors: 其他三个选项不是作者的建议，故均排除。

parts.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words (not including the sentence given).

reference.shenTi: 题目要求考生写一篇以"人们普遍认为，获得扎实的基础知识对学生掌握一门学科至关重要"开头的作文，考生可以通过发表评论、举例子或描述个人经历展开作文。根据题目提示，作文可以采取以下布局：开头段表明个人立场，即完全同意这一观点；中间段列出具体论据；结尾段总结全文。考生写作时可以使用与"说明重要性""阐述原因"相关的写作句型。
reference.modelEssay:
As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject. I fully agree with the above opinion. I have two arguments to support it.
First of all, learning the basics helps students be prepared to master an academic subject. As everyone knows, learning is a step-by-step process. Students should start with the basic knowledge of an academic subject before they are able to reach a higher level. Moreover, the knowledge of the basics contains the universal law of a subject, which can be applied to different branches of the academic subject. Thus gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is necessary for mastering the knowledge of various branches of the academic subject.
In conclusion, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is extremely important for students to master an academic subject. It can not only help students be prepared for the future study but also help them master the knowledge of different branches of the academic subject.
reference.essayTranslation:
人们普遍认为，获得扎实的基础知识对学生掌握一门学科至关重要。我完全同意上述观点。我有两个理由来支持这一观点。
首先，学习基础知识有助于学生为掌握一门学科做好准备。众所周知，学习是一个循序渐进的过程。学生应该从一门学科的基础知识开始，然后才能达到更高的水平。此外，基础知识包含了一门学科的一般规律，可以适用于该学科的不同分科。因此，获得扎实的基础知识对于掌握该学科各个分科的知识是必要的。
总之，获得扎实的基础知识对于学生掌握一门学科是极其重要的。它不仅可以帮助学生为以后的学习做好准备，还可以帮助他们掌握该学科不同分科的知识。
reference.commentary: [1]表明个人立场，即完全同意"获得扎实的基础知识对学生掌握一门学科至关重要"这一观点。[2]分别从"为掌握一门学科做好准备"和"基础知识适用于该学科的不同分科"论证上述观点，由连接词First of all和Moreover引出。[3]总结全文，重申观点。
highlightedExpressions: reach a higher level 达到更高的水平

parts.sourceZh: 在中国，随着老龄化社会的到来，养老受到普遍关注。人们谈论最多的是应当采取什么样的养老模式。多数人认为，养老模式需要多元化。可以通过政府引导和社会参与，建立更多更好的养老服务机构，改进社区服务中心，鼓励居家自助养老，还可以推行家庭养老与社会养老相结合的模式。随着政府和社会对养老服务事业投入的持续增加，养老设施将不断升级，服务质量逐步改进，老年人的生活将会更加方便舒适、健康快乐。

reference.referenceEn: In China, with the arrival of an aging society, the elderly care has received widespread attention. What people talk about the most is what kind of elderly care model should be adopted. Most people believe that the elderly care model needs to be diversified. Through government guidance and social participation, we can establish more and better elderly care service institutions, improve community service centers, encourage home-based self-help elderly care, and promote a model combining family and social elderly care. With the increasing investment in elderly care services from the government and society, elderly care facilities will continue to be upgraded, service quality will be gradually improved, and the elderly will live a more convenient, more comfortable, healthier and happier life.
